trust_decision.summary: The plugin trusts that @fastify/send neutralises a non-leading '..' segment in the pathname it is handed, but send normalises '..' away before its own guard runs, so a request whose raw path normalises onto a guarded or otherwise unrouted prefix is served from disk anyway; the decision is taken where the wildcard handler turns req.raw.url into a pathname (index.js:142) and the assumption is consumed at the single send() call (index.js:291).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('route guard bypass via path traversal') points at the wildcard GET/HEAD route handler, which is the only place that derives a filesystem pathname from the request URL; an engineer reads getPathnameForSend() first and sees there is no dot-dot check at all.

fix_sites.entry_point: all three: GET/HEAD `prefix + '*'` route, reply.sendFile, reply.download
reply.sendFile (index.js:97-109) and reply.download (index.js:111-125), both via pumpSendToReply
GET/HEAD `prefix + '*'` route, incl. prefix with a route param ('/app/:version')
reply path of both rejected sites (403 body)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: reply.sendFile/reply.download are called by the application with a path the developer picked, so a solver argues the report's route-guard bypass is an app-trust boundary and not the plugin's job; likewise the '/app/:version' mount that consumes the '..' into a route param is an unusual configuration the report never names.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Directory redirect and slash collapsing must keep working: a path whose last segment is '.' still has to be treated as a directory and redirected (the fix's own test adds '/deep/path/for/test/.' -> 301) and repeated slashes must still serve ('///deep/path//for//test//index.html' -> 200); an over-broad fix that rejects any dot segment, or that path.normalize()s the pathname before send, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: '..' consumed by a route param before the suffix is computed: /app/../deep/... with prefix '/app/:version'
'..' passed to the programmatic API: reply.sendFile('foo/../index.html')
leading '..' deliberately left to @fastify/send (excluded from the new rejection)
backslash-separated '..\\' (regex accepts both separators, not covered by a test)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a dot-dot segment rejection added inside dirList.path next to the existing isPathInsideRoot guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dirList.path already turns a route into a filesystem path and already refuses escapes, so a maintainer fixing traversal would plausibly tighten it there, which would cover only the directory-list route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a copy of the pathname check in setUpHeadAndGet/serveFileHandler for the wildcard:false mode
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: wildcard:false is a second, route-per-file implementation of the same serve path with its own handler and route config, so guarding it separately looks natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: findIndexFile(), which reaches the filesystem with path.join(root, pathname, filename)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: index resolution is a second filesystem reach inside the same pump, so a maintainer could put the check here to protect directory requests.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared FST_STATIC_FORBIDDEN_PATH @fastify/error class instead of the inline forbiddenPathError()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every other plugin error is a createError class in lib/errors.js (imported at index.js:15-19), so a maintainer would naturally add the 403 there and could then wire it into only one of the two call sites.

O10_build.toolchain: npm; borp test runner with c8 line-coverage gate; eslint (neostandard); tstyche for types
O10_build.project_tests: test/static.test.js (large; already asserts '/static/../index.js' -> 404 at test/static.test.js:184-191 and the redirect matrix at test/static.test.js:3554-3598) and test/dir-list.test.js (raw-socket traversal tests expecting 403, test/dir-list.test.js:226-270); run with `npm run test:unit`. Note the fix's own tests had to add a raw node:http helper (fix.diff:95-117) because fetch/URL normalises '..' away before the request is sent, while test/dir-list.test.js:24-33 already had such a helper.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the dot-dot rejection once, either at the wildcard handler's pathname or at the send() call, but the handler-level check misses reply.sendFile/reply.download entirely while the sink-level check cannot see a '..' the route-prefix matcher already consumed into a route param - both are needed, with different inputs.

out_of_scope_notes: The root cause sits one layer below this repository: @fastify/send normalises non-leading '..' before its own guard (stated in the fix comment at fix.diff:34-35); that dependency is not in the pinned tree and is not pursued.
